Reporting network test results

Source: R/report_tests.R
report_tests.Rd

These methods report a network_test, the result of test_random(), test_configuration(), test_permutation(), test_gof(), test_distributions(), test_parameter(), and test_time().

  • print() shows a title that says what was tested, a blank line, tidy() of the result, and a footer that says how the null distribution was made and the controls that differ from the default. For a test whose statistic is a distance, from test_gof(), test_distributions(), test_parameter(), or test_time(), only the upper tail is a p-value, and only it is marked.

  • tidy() and glance() give the same as a tibble of one row, after {broom}.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'network_test'
tidy(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'network_test'
glance(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'network_test'
print(x, ..., max.length = 6, digits = 3)

Arguments

x

A network_test.

...

Not used.

max.length, digits

Not used.

Value

print() returns x, invisibly. tidy() and glance() give one row with the observed statistic, the mean and standard deviation of the null distribution, and the share of the null distribution at or below (p.lower) and at or above (p.upper) the observed statistic. For test_gof() and test_distributions(), the statistic is a distance, the null distribution is that of the reference simulations, and p.upper is the p-value.

Examples

qaptest <- test_permutation(manynet::ison_adolescents,
                            netrics::net_by_density, times = 20)
print(qaptest)
#> # QAP test of netrics::net_by_density()
#> 
#> # A tibble: 1 × 5
#>   statistic null.mean null.sd p.lower p.upper
#>       <dbl>     <dbl>   <dbl> <chr>   <chr>  
#> 1     0.357     0.357       0 1       1      
#> 
#> # Null: 20 permutations of the node labels.
tidy(qaptest)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 7
#>   method statistic null.mean null.sd p.lower p.upper times
#>   <chr>      <dbl>     <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 QAP        0.357     0.357       0       1       1    20
